name: Frame-time budget view in the debug window
body: Dean (2026-11-20): engine-level work. Show where each frame's time goes against the 16.6 ms budget for 60 fps: per-phase timings, a rolling graph and a clear over-budget indicator, in the debug window. Overhead must be tiny while the window is hidden.
details: Outcome (2026-11-20): FrameBudget in engine/src/core, Budget page in the debug window (graph of 120 frames against 16.7 ms, per-phase values, over-budget heading, caps and counts), phases timed only while the window shows. See docs/debug-window.md and D-224. Screenshot posted to the project chat.
plan: A Budget page in the debug window (after Frame). The loop and GameHost time each phase with the monotonic clock (events, fixed update with physics, script update, UI, animation and draw extraction, render, audio, the debug window itself) only while the window is visible. FrameBudget keeps a 120-frame ring per phase; the page draws one stacked bar per frame against a 16.6 ms line, bars turn red over budget, with a per-phase table (this frame, average, worst) and an over-budget count. Phases published as Budget/ values too, so they are filterable.
acceptance_criteria: Budget page shows per-phase times for update, scripting, physics, render and audio
A rolling graph of the last 120 frames against the 16.6 ms budget
Over-budget frames are marked clearly (colour, line and a count)
Nothing is measured while the debug window is hidden
definition_of_done: Tests added and `mist run test` passes
Screenshot posted to the project chat
